newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait to ask for higher OPEC quota at right time.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait to ask for higher OPEC quota at right time.

text.p: Kuwait will ask for a higher OPEC quota at the appropriate time, the Gulf Arab state's oil minister said in an interview published on Saturday.

Isa al-Mazeedi told al-Anba newspaper the two million barrel per day (bpd) OPEC quota "does not meet Kuwait's just demands for a higher quota in line with production capacity, historical market share, reserves...".
Kuwait has repeatedly said it deserves a higher Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries quota of about 200,000 bpd. It says its production capacity currently stands at 2.5 million bpd.

"Kuwait will reiterate its demands for a higher quota if circumstances permit," said Mazeedi who was appointed in October, adding that Kuwait plans to achieve a three million bpd production capacity by 2005.
"We are optimistic about world oil prices amid positive indicators which will help prices stay at reasonable levels," said the minister.
In 1996 Kuwaiti crudes averaged about $5 a barrel higher than the $13 a barrel used to calculate oil revenue in the budget.
